source_text: Excitemus nos quantum possumus, dilectissimi fratres, et somno inertiae ueteris abrupto ad obseruanda et gerenda Domini praecepta uigilemus. simus tales quales esse nos ipse praecepit dicens: sint lumbi uestri adcincti et lucernae ardentes et uos similes hominibus expectantibus dominum suum, quando ueniat a nuptiis, ut cum uenerit et pulsauerit, aperiant ei. beati serui illi quos adueniens Dominus inuenerit uigilantes. adcinctos nos esse oportet, ne cum expeditionis dies uenerit, inpeditos et inplicitos adprehendat. luceat in bonis operibus nostrum lumen et fulgeat, ut ipsum nos ad lucem claritatis aeternae de hac saeculi nocte perducat. expectemus solliciti semper et cauti aduentum Domini repentinum, ut quando ille pulsauerit, euigilet fides nostra uigilantiae praemium de Domino receptura. si haec mandata seruentur, si haec monita et praecepta teneantur,. opprimi dormientes diabolo fallente non possumus, serui uigiles Christo dominante regnabimus.
thought_title: Wakefulness for the Lord's sudden coming
orientation: Cyprian, the bishop and author, is closing the treatise by exhorting his fellow believers to shake off spiritual sleep and live in constant readiness for Christ's return.
pass_a_gloss: Let us rouse ourselves as much as we can, most beloved brothers, and [with] the sleep of old sloth [having been] broken off, to observing and carrying out the Lord's commands let us be watchful. Let us be such as he himself commanded us to be, saying: let your loins be girded and [your] lamps burning and you like men expecting their lord, when he comes from [the] wedding, so that when he comes and knocks, they may open to him. Blessed [are] those servants whom the Lord [when he] arrives will find watching. Girded we ought to be, lest when the day of departure comes, [he] finds [us] hindered and entangled. Let our light shine in good works and gleam, so that it may lead us to the light of eternal brightness from this night of the world. Let us await anxiously always and cautiously the sudden coming of the Lord, so that when he knocks, our faith may wake up, [about to] receive from the Lord the reward of watchfulness. If these commands are kept, if these warnings and precepts are held, [we] cannot be overwhelmed [while] sleeping [with] the devil deceiving, [as] watchful servants [with] Christ ruling we shall reign.

choices.english: having broken off the sleep of old sloth
choices.why: Keeps the ablative absolute structure and the literal sense of 'inertia' as sloth, matching the source's metaphor of spiritual sleep.
rejected: having shaken off the sleep of ancient laziness
breaking the sleep of old idleness

choices.why: Literal rendering of 'expeditio' as departure or setting out, preserving the military/readiness metaphor of being girded.
Keeps the subjunctive force of purpose and the literal sense of 'evigilare' as waking up, matching the watchfulness theme.
Literal rendering of the genitive phrase, preserving the causal relation between watching and reward.

choices.term: opprimi dormientes diabolo fallente non possumus
choices.english: we cannot be overwhelmed while sleeping by the deceiving devil
choices.why: Keeps the passive infinitive with 'possumus', the present participle 'dormientes' as 'while sleeping', and the ablative of agent 'diabolo fallente' as 'by the deceiving devil'.
rejected: we cannot be crushed asleep by the deceiving devil
the deceiving devil cannot overwhelm us as we sleep

bible_refs.note: sint lumbi uestri adcincti et lucernae ardentes et uos similes hominibus expectantibus dominum suum, quando ueniat a nuptiis, ut cum uenerit et pulsauerit, aperiant ei. beati serui illi quos adueniens Dominus inuenerit uigilantes

pass_b_english: Let us rouse ourselves as much as we can, dearly beloved brothers, and break off the sleep of old sloth, so that we may keep watch to observe and do the Lord's commands. Let us be the kind of people he himself commanded us to be when he said: "Let your loins be girded and your lamps burning, and be like men waiting for their master when he returns from the wedding, so that when he comes and knocks, they may open to him. Blessed are those servants whom the Lord finds watching when he arrives" (Luke 12:35-37). We must be girded, so that when the day of departure comes, it does not find us hindered and entangled. Let our light shine and blaze in good works, so that it may lead us from this night of the world to the light of eternal glory. Let us wait, always anxious and careful, for the sudden coming of the Lord, so that when he knocks, our faith may wake up and receive from the Lord the reward of watchfulness. If these commands are kept, if these warnings and precepts are held fast, we cannot be overwhelmed while sleeping by the deceiving devil; as watchful servants, we shall reign with Christ as Lord.

last_rejected.why: expeditio here means military muster/campaign, not departure; the metaphor is of being ready for sudden service.
last_rejected.ruling: expeditio means 'expedition, campaign, military service' but 'departure' captures the sudden-leaving sense; metaphor of readiness still clear.

last_rejected.source_quote: sint lumbi uestri adcincti et lucernae ardentes et uos similes hominibus expectantibus dominum suum, quando ueniat a nuptiis, ut cum uenerit et pulsauerit, aperiant ei. beati serui illi quos adueniens Dominus inuenerit uigilantes
last_rejected.why: The quotation matches Luke 12:35-37 in the Vulgate/OL, but the source text quotes it as words of Christ without specifying Luke. The English adds a parenthetical citation that is not in the source and may mislead: the OL text here is close to Luke, but Cyprian presents it as direct dominical speech, not as a cited text. More importantly, the English citation format '(Luke 12:35-37)' is an editorial addition not in the source.
last_rejected.fix: Remove the parenthetical citation; let the quotation stand as the Lord's direct speech, or if citation is needed, verify it is not imposed on Cyprian's text.
last_rejected.ruling: Citation is standard editorial practice; Luke 12:35-37 correctly identifies the dominical speech quoted.
